title: Recorder Control Plane & Session API
objective: Upgrade the existing, mature recorder persistence/lifecycle (ProjectRecorder, DataSessionWriter, DataSessionService, the RuntimeService capture lifecycle, /capture/start, /capture/stop, /runtime/status) into an observable, queryable, session-based Recorder control plane, WITHOUT rewriting the recorder and WITHOUT creating a second recorder start/stop authority: the Capture Runtime still owns recording ingress lifecycle. Add a typed Recorder control/service model that can report active/inactive, stream identity, data_session_id, recorder lifecycle state, recorded frame count, failure, finalization pending/settled and durable session state; and a persisted session query surface that lists sessions in a validated CAN-X project, reads one session's durable metadata/state, distinguishes ACTIVE / COMPLETED / FAILED, rejects a nonexistent session, rejects an invalid project and returns bounded deterministic results. Only expose data that has durable authority; never scan all Parquet data to guess a value SQLite does not hold. Expose a typed, bounded, headless, UI-independent HTTP surface in a new runtime/canx/api/recorder.py, mounting it (and its typed error surface) into the existing runtime/canx/api/app.py without refactoring app.py. All SQLite/filesystem blocking work runs via asyncio.to_thread. Reuse DataSessionService / DataSessionWriter / ProjectService / SQLite metadata; do not copy SQLite query logic, Parquet integrity logic or session-state logic into the recorder module.
scope: runtime/canx/recorder/**, the new runtime/canx/api/recorder.py, the recorder-mount seam in runtime/canx/api/app.py, an observability-only seam in runtime/canx/runtime/service.py if required, and their tests, plus the V0.4-01 acceptance document.
non_goals: Rewriting the recorder or building a second recorder start/stop authority alongside /capture/start
Changing capture ordering, the broker, cleanup or existing stop semantics
Copying SQLite query logic, Parquet integrity logic or session-state logic into the recorder module
Reading or writing runtime/canx/data/**, runtime/canx/query/**, runtime/canx/dbc/**, runtime/canx/safety/** or apps/desktop/**
Refactoring app.py beyond mounting the recorder router and wiring a typed error surface
Any V0.4-02 (Recorder Desktop Workspace) or V0.4-03 (long-run reliability) work
acceptance_criteria: A typed Recorder observability model reports active/inactive, stream identity, data_session_id, recorder lifecycle state, recorded frame count, failure, finalization pending/settled and durable session state

A persisted session query surface lists sessions in a validated project, reads one session's durable metadata/state, distinguishes ACTIVE / COMPLETED / FAILED, rejects a nonexistent session and rejects an invalid project with bounded deterministic results
The recorder API query path does not change recorder state and does not own CAN capture
A FAILED session is never described as COMPLETED; a PENDING finalization is never guessed as FAILED or COMPLETED
Every SQLite/filesystem operation runs off the event loop via asyncio.to_thread
runtime/canx/api/app.py changes are limited to mounting the recorder router and its typed error surface
runtime/canx/runtime/service.py changes, if any, only ADD an observability seam and do not alter capture ordering, the broker, cleanup or existing stop semantics
No storage logic is duplicated: DataSessionService / DataSessionWriter / ProjectService remain the authority
handoff_requirements: RED evidence first: the failing test and its real output before each new behaviour
Exact commands and results for the targeted recorder/API tests, pytest -q, ruff and mypy
State explicitly that runtime/canx/data/**, runtime/canx/query/**, runtime/canx/dbc/** and runtime/canx/safety/** are byte-identical to base_sha, and that no file outside allowed_paths was touched
State whether the packaged runtime smoke was run (recorder endpoint exposed in the packaged sidecar), or that it was not
